newsitem.title: USA: Beverly comfortable with analysts estimates.
newsitem.headline: Beverly comfortable with analysts estimates.

text.p: Beverly Enterprises Inc's chief executive David Banks Thursday told analysts he expects annual earnings to increase by at least 15 percent and that he is comfortable with analysts' earnings projections for the full year.
A company spokesman said, in a telephone interview with Reuters, that Banks made the statement on a conference call with analysts, following the company's press release Thursday on its earnings.

A First Call consensus estimate put the company's earnings at $0.88 a share for the full year. Most estimates fall between $0.88 and $0.90 per share, the company spokesman said. The company reported $0.76 per share for 1996.

"We expect earnings to increase by at least 15 percent a year," Banks stated according to the spokesman. Banks added: "We do not see slower growth ahead and we do not see any slowdown in our annual earnings."
Banks earlier today said in a statement that he believed the company would meet or exceed its internal financial targets for the year.

"The gains we expect to make during the second half will be somewhat smaller in scale (than the 28 percent earnings increase the company posted in the first half), reflecting the fact that we'll be compairing our improved performance with the agressive results we achieved in the third and fourth quarter of 1996," he said in the statement.
Beverly reported earnings of $39.4 million, or $0.40 a share, for the first six months of the year, a 28 percent increase over the first half of 1997.
